_comment: FLAT ground-truth solve of the 114-node fine SCATTERED topology, oracle for the scattered hierarchical run. Same cost warning as the clustered flat input.
_expected: Host-uplink bound T* >= 0.880 s = 44 epochs, set by the 8-GPU hosts (704 GB across the host boundary / 800 GB/s of dual-plane egress). The spine cut is SLACK at 0.640 s, which is the whole point of a non-blocking fabric -- so LATENCY SHOULD TIE between clustered and scattered. The comparison lives in objective_type 5's switch-hop tie-breaker term: scattered puts 33.3% of cross-host GPU pairs on a shared leaf vs clustered's 22.6%, so scattered should show strictly FEWER leaf->spine hops at the same makespan. A latency DIFFERENCE means something is wrong (or an uplink got tapered). num_epochs is pinned to 64, same as the clustered flat input, so the two flat solves are comparable.
_epoch_note: epoch_duration is PINNED to 0.02 s (= 1/50 GB/s, the fine GPU->leaf link) rather than derived, and this is load-bearing for the A/B. Derived SLOWEST_LINK sizing would give the two placements DIFFERENT epochs -- SLOWEST_LINK reads the MIN coarse capacity, which is 400 GB/s clustered vs 100 GB/s scattered -- a 4x difference in quantum, giving 0.0025 s vs 0.0100 s -- so the makespans would differ by epoch quantization rather than by placement quality. Same epoch on both sides is what makes the comparison mean anything.
_known_failure: The coarse LP can trip account_for_consume's 'assert consume == 0' on sub-feasibility-tol Gurobi flow noise (see the lp_extraction_feasibility_tol_noise note). feasibility_tol is tightened to 1e-6 here to make that less likely; if it still fires, that is the known extraction bug, not a topology problem.
